scenario: Brake warning light on or pedal feels soft
action_plan: DO: Reduce speed gradually and pull over safely as soon as possible. Activate hazard lights. Use the handbrake / parking brake to slow if foot brake fails. Call recovery — do not drive further. DO NOT: Continue driving with a brake warning light to 'reach a garage'; do not pump the pedal repeatedly hoping to restore pressure; do not assume it's just low brake fluid until inspected.

scenario: Water leaking from indoor AC unit or air handler
action_plan: DO: Switch off the AC at the breaker. Place a container under the leak. Check for an obvious blocked condensate drain at the unit (often a small white pipe). Move belongings from beneath. DO NOT: Tape over the drain pan; do not run the AC while it's leaking; do not open the unit's casing or refrigerant lines.

scenario: Chemical or sweet smell from AC vents (possible refrigerant leak)
action_plan: DO: Switch off the AC at the breaker or fuse spur immediately. Open windows and ventilate fully. Leave the affected area — refrigerant exposure can cause dizziness, breathing difficulty, and frostbite on direct contact. Call an F-Gas / EPA 608 certified engineer urgently. DO NOT: Continue running the AC; do not investigate the source yourself; do not seal the unit or vents.
